articles.title: Telangana sets up special probe into Dharani irregularities
articles.description:
Telangana : The Telangana government is preparing to constitute a Special Enquiry Team (SET) to conduct a comprehensive probe into alleged irregularities in the Dharani land records portal. The decision follows a forensic audit of the portal, which has reportedly identified more than [...]Telangana : The Telangana government is preparing to constitute a Special Enquiry Team (SET) to conduct a comprehensive probe into alleged irregularities in the Dharani land records portal. The team will comprise officials from the Police, Revenue and Information Technology departments.

The decision follows a forensic audit of the portal, which has reportedly identified more than 10,000 suspicious transactions since Dharani became operational. The investigation will examine the portal's software architecture, operational processes and alleged manipulation of land records.

Notices likely to IL&FS, Terra CIS over portal management

The government is expected to issue notices first to IL&FS and its associated company, Terra CIS Technologies Limited, which handled the design, development and maintenance of the Dharani portal. The inquiry will seek explanations on digital record alterations, alleged data security lapses and the tender process through which the project was awarded.

The SET will also scrutinise agreements between the companies, the extent of their responsibilities, fund flows and compliance with contractual obligations. Investigators will examine whether the tender process adhered to government rules and whether the system architecture contained vulnerabilities that enabled misuse.

The probe will assess whether contractual terms governing a project funded with public money were violated and determine whether legal action is warranted against those found responsible.

Team to examine land classification changes and data access

The Special Enquiry Team will review every digital transaction carried out through the Dharani portal, including login records of officials who accessed or modified land data.

The investigation will focus on changes made to land records over the past few years, approvals granted for those changes and the process through which land was shifted from the prohibited list to the general category. Police, Revenue and IT officials will jointly analyse system logs to identify the login IDs used for record modifications and trace those responsible.

Investigators will also examine whether private entities or vendors were granted unauthorised access to digitised land records, leading to misuse of sensitive land data. As part of the inquiry, officials will collect bank account details of beneficiaries linked to suspicious transactions, registration documents and other records to verify whether government or private lands were illegally transferred.

Cyber Crime experts from the Police department will assist the SET in tracing every digital signature and system click associated with the more than 10,000 suspicious transactions identified during the forensic audit.

The team will also investigate the basis on which prohibited lands were reclassified, identify individuals who allegedly benefited from the changes and examine the role of technical personnel involved. A comprehensive report will be submitted to the state government after the inquiry is completed. ]]>

articles.title: 30.6 GW and Counting: India's H1 Renewable Number Gets an Official Seal With a Solar Surge to Match
articles.description: Total renewable capacity, including hydro, now stands at 288 GW as of June 30 — 52% of India's entire installed base, per Central Electricity Authority data. Solar's 26.34 GW of H1 additions represents a striking acceleration from the same period a year earlier, and pushes cumulative solar capacity to 162 GW; wind stands at 57 GW. Solar and wind together now account for close to 219 GW, or roughly 93% of non-hydro renewable capacity — a concentration that says as much about what has worked (utility tenders, ALMM-driven manufacturing, falling technology costs) as about what has lagged (biomass, small hydro, geothermal's still-nascent pilots). External agencies confirm the trend as well. The International Energy Agency's latest assessment, cited alongside the government numbers, found India's 2025 annual renewable additions rose nearly 60% — the fastest growth among major global markets — with almost 50 GW of solar PV commissioned, twice the prior year's pace, and wind additions more than doubling past 6 GW. The IEA's one caveat is a familiar one to readers of this publication: offshore wind projects continue to stall on cancellations and delays, a segment where India's ambition and its execution remain furthest apart. State-level detail sharpens the picture further. Gujarat has cemented itself as India's renewable powerhouse, with a combined solar-and-wind installed base of over 49 GW. More than 22% of the national solar-plus-wind total, split between 33.2 GW of solar and 16.1 GW of wind. Rajasthan continues to anchor utility-scale solar deployment at gigawatt scale, while Tamil Nadu and Karnataka have built the more balanced solar-wind portfolios that hybrid and FDRE tenders increasingly reward. What should temper any premature celebrations is the parallel story breaking this week: the Northern Regional Power Committee's directive to developers, inverter manufacturers and controller suppliers following repeated instances of sudden generation loss in the region — precisely the kind of grid-stability friction that accelerating solar concentration produces. Half of India's renewable fleet now sits in a small number of high-density clusters across Gujarat, Rajasthan and the northern grid; the faster that capacity grows, the less tolerance the system has of any single technical weak point. The H1 number is a genuine achievement and should be read as one. But 30.6 GW added in six months is also 30.6 GW of new integration burden for a grid that is beginning to struggle. The honest frame for the second half, then, is not whether India can keep adding gigawatts at this pace - the pipeline, the manufacturing base and the tender machinery all suggest it can, but whether the grid architecture, the regulatory penalty framework taking shape for 2027, and the storage buildout can mature at the same speed. India has comprehensively won the argument about whether renewables can scale in this country. The argument now underway is about whether they can be trusted to behave once they do.

articles.title: Bondada Wins NTPC REL's 100 MWh VRFB BESS Project with Delectrik as Tech Partner
articles.description: Bondada Engineering has secured its first and largest grid-scale Vanadium Redox Flow Battery (VRFB) Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project. The company has been awarded the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) package for a 16.7 MW/100 MWh VRFB BESS project. The project was tendered in February this year and has now been awarded after five months. In a regulatory filing, the company said it has received a Notification of Award (NOA) from NTPC Renewable Energy Limited (NTPC REL) to execute the Vanadium Redox Flow Battery Energy Storage System (VRFB BESS) at Khavda Solar Park, Gujarat. The project marks a significant milestone for Bondada Engineering and aligns with its strategy to execute energy storage projects based on advanced Long Duration Energy Storage (LDES) technologies. Delectrik Systems Joins as Technology Partner Under the scope of work, Bondada Engineering Limited will execute the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) package, with Delectrik Systems Pvt Ltd serving as the technology partner. This is not the first time Delectrik Systems , a flow battery OEM, has won a tender from NTPC. The company won a project in 2023 for NETRA (NTPC Energy Technology Research Alliance) to develop a 3 MWh Vanadium Redox Flow Battery (VRFB)-based Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The system was deployed in the first half of 2025 at the NETRA campus in Greater Noida, India. Delectrik won the tender in collaboration with Rays Power Infra, an EPC company that has commissioned over 1.5 GWp of solar projects across India and Southeast Asia (SE Asia). The project will deploy Vanadium Redox Flow Battery (VRFB) technology, an energy storage solution that offers several advantages over conventional Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) battery systems. While LFP batteries largely depend on imported cells and typically have an operational life of 12–15 years, VRFB technology offers a significantly longer service life of more than 25 years, along with high intrinsic safety, stable performance under frequent cycling with near-zero degradation, and lower operational expenditure. Furthermore, India possesses domestic vanadium resources, making VRFB technology an attractive option for reducing long-term import dependence while supporting the Government's vision of strengthening indigenous energy security. Scope of Work Under the scope of work, the contractor will obtain site-specific data from the owner to prepare installation and implementation plans. It will also be responsible for supplying all equipment, components, and services required to install a fully functional BESS. The BESS capacity will be based on the rated AC discharge capacity at the point of injection or metering and will be integrated at the 33 kV pooling substation of the solar plant. The tender also requires the contractor to undertake comprehensive Operations and Maintenance (O&M) of the BESS for 10 years from the date of successful commissioning. In addition, grid compliance studies, reactive power compensation, and power quality compliance for the entire BESS system up to the 400 kV grid interconnection point at the NTPC REL project switchyard will fall within the contractor's scope. Aligning With Govt's 236 GWh BESS Target The Government of India has set an ambitious target of deploying approximately 236 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems by 2030, while the country's current installed capacity stands at only around 3.3 GWh. This highlights the significant growth opportunity in the Indian energy storage market, driven by the rapid expansion of renewable energy capacity and the increasing need for grid stability. The project further strengthens Bondada Engineering's position in the rapidly expanding BESS sector, complementing its existing renewable energy EPC portfolio. The company said it remains committed to supporting India's energy transition by delivering innovative, sustainable, and technologically advanced infrastructure solutions. Bondada Engineering added that it will continue to focus on next-generation technologies and actively participate in the development of India's fast-growing clean energy ecosystem, creating long-term value for all stakeholders.

articles.title: Plea moved in SC over HC refusal to probe Adani green contracts
articles.description: A petition has been filed in the Supreme Court challenging the refusal by the Bombay high court to probe procurement of energy contracts with states by Adani Green Energy Limited using alleged unlawful means
